newsitem.title: USA: Digital to make statement within hour.
newsitem.headline: Digital to make statement within hour.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp on Wednesday said it would release a statment within an hour about its contractual agreement with Intel Corp and a counter-lawsuit filed by Intel.
"There will be a statement within an hour," a spokeswoman for Digital told Reuters.

Intel said on Wednesday it filed a lawsuit against Digital, alleging Digital has refused to return confidential information. Intel also said its contract to supply its Pentium family of chips to Digital expires after the third quarter of 1997, rather than June 30, 1999, as Digital has asserted.
In a statement earlier today, Intel said it sought return of "confidential information pertaining to Intel's products that it has transferred to DEC over the past several years."

Digital said Intel's demands related to materials that Intel shared with Digital and other vendors that use Intel processors in their products. Digital also said it did not expect to be deprived of access to those products.
"We expect to have timely access to Intel technology," Siekman said. "This counter suit is nothing more than a thinly veiled attempt to cause concern among Digital customers."
"There has been no disruption of supply of product from Intel and we expect none in the future," Siekman said. "We have product agreements with Intel that run until 1999."

"The simple fact is that our suit was filed because we discovered that Intel, without permission, is using Digital patented technology to gain significant performance improvements in their products and we want them to stop," Siekman said.
"Since Intel's use of our technology is unlawful, they are attempting to threaten and silence us," Siekman said. "It won't work and we are confident that we will win."
